headline: Gartner, a business research firm, estimates that more than $3.5 trillion of AI computing and data centre spending could have to be written down by the end of 2030.
score_reason: Facts match the headline; it is a single firm's forecast built on stated assumptions.
importance_line: Investors in AI infrastructure and lenders to data centre builders are most affected, then the small AI cloud firms called neoclouds; the doubt is that this is a forecast resting on Gartner's assumptions, including a 12% return hurdle.
summary: Gartner says AI providers are expected to spend nearly $1 trillion on AI infrastructure in 2026 and about $6 trillion more from 2027 to 2030, while revenue attributable to AI data centres is forecast at no more than $3.6 trillion against the $8.5 trillion owners would need to cover costs and earn a 12% return. Will Sommer, a senior director analyst at Gartner, says that leaves more than $3.5 trillion exposed to write-downs and that over 80% of neocloud providers, firms that rent out AI computing, will cease independent operations by 2030.
notes: Read in CXOToday's copy of the Gartner statement, so Gartner is credited as the source with CXOToday as carrier. Same Gartner report as C07-06; the editor may merge or cross-link the two.
